Article Title: Abhishek strikes with 45 seconds left as India pip Pakistan 4-3 to enter Asian Games hockey gold-medal match
Article Text:
Image credit: Hockey India

Harmanpreet puts India in control

Pakistan find a way back

Pakistan complete the comeback

Abhishek has the final say

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India survived a huge scare against Pakistan before Abhishek scored with just 45 seconds left to give the defending champions a dramatic 4-3 win in the Asian Games hockey semifinal on Thursday.The victory sends India into the hockey gold medal match, while Pakistan will play for the bronze medal.India will take on the winner of the second semifinal between Malaysia and Korea.Just when the semifinal looked set for a shootout, Abhishek produced the winning moment. His effort took a deflection off Pakistan defender Sufiyan and went past goalkeeper Ali Raza to send India into the gold-medal match.India will face the winner of the second semifinal between South Korea and Malaysia.India started on the front foot and kept Pakistan under pressure from the opening minutes.After failing to convert their first four penalty corners, India finally broke the deadlock in the fifth minute. Captain Harmanpreet stepped up and fired a powerful drag-flick past goalkeeper Ali Raza to make it 1-0.Harmanpreet struck again in the 13th minute. Manpreet Singh's run down the left helped India win their seventh penalty corner, and the captain made no mistake.India were now firmly in control and Pakistan struggled to find a way into the game.Sukhjeet then made it 3-0 in the 23rd minute. Shilanand Lakra sent a fine pass from the left of the goal-line and Sukhjeet finished the move.India appeared to have one foot in the final.Pakistan, however, got a much-needed goal just before half-time.Abu Mahmood scored from a penalty corner in the 30th minute to reduce the deficit to 1-3 and give Pakistan hope.India continued to attack after the break. Dilpreet Singh and Hardik Singh helped India create chances, while Abhishek came close to scoring in the 40th minute when his flick hit the far post.That miss soon became important.Pakistan grew in confidence and started putting India's defence under pressure. Hannan Shahid scored in the 45th minute after receiving a pass from Ali Ghazanfar to make it 2-3.The goal changed the mood of the match. Pakistan were suddenly on top, while India struggled to regain control.India were forced to play with 10 men for a period after Dilpreet was shown a green card in the 43rd minute.Pakistan used the opportunity to keep attacking and eventually found the equaliser.Hannan set up Waheed Rana in the 49th minute and Rana finished the chance to make it 3-3.From being three goals ahead, India were suddenly facing the possibility of a shootout.Pakistan continued to push forward in the final stages, while India were forced to defend deep. The Indian defence and goalkeeper made important saves to keep the score level.India also had a video referral for a penalty corner, but the appeal was turned down.With the clock running down, India finally found their moment.Abhishek got his stick to the ball near the goalmouth with just 45 seconds remaining. The ball took a deflection off Sufiyan and wrong-footed Ali Raza before finding the back of the net.India had their 4-3 lead back.Pakistan tried to find another equaliser in the final seconds, but India held on to complete a dramatic victory.The defending champions had dominated the first half and built a 3-0 lead, but Pakistan's three-goal comeback exposed India's struggles after the break.In the end, Abhishek's late goal ensured India avoided a shootout and booked their place in the Asian Games hockey gold-medal match.
Article Summary: Defending champions India beat Pakistan 4-3 in the Asian Games hockey semifinal. Abhishek scored with just 45 seconds left to give the defending champions a dramatic win. The victory sends India into the hockey gold medal match, while Pakistan will play for the bronze medal.

Article Title: After Asiad row, Manika set to return to domestic circuit after four years amid ranking uncertainty
Article Text:
Manika Batra (Image: IANS)

NEW DELHI: Four years after her last appearance in a domestic tournament, India’s leading paddler Manika Batra is set to return to the national circuit, with the 31-year-old entering the National Ranking Table Tennis Championships in Panchkula , Haryana, scheduled from Octo 6 to 13.TOI has learnt that Manika has officially submitted her entry for the tournament, which will mark her first domestic appearance since the Senior Nationals in Shillong in April 2022. Batra had then lost to Ayhika Mukherjee in the pre-quarterfinals.Her return assumes added significance after her omission from India’s main squad for the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. Manika, who was ranked world No. 51 and was India’s second-highest ranked women’s player at the time, was named among the reserves after her absence from domestic competitions meant she did not have the national ranking points required under the selection criteria.Manika had questioned the selection process following her omission and sought clarity from the authorities, including the sports ministry and Indian Olympic Association. Her decision to re-enter the domestic circuit now comes as the sport looks towards the next Olympic qualification cycle and the 2028 Los Angeles Games.However, the Panchkula tournament is facing an unusual situation of its own. The newly appointed ad-hoc committee overseeing table tennis has withdrawn official ranking points from upcoming National Ranking tournaments following the suspension of the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) on Aug12, it has been learnt.The development has created uncertainty for players who had planned their domestic schedules around the ranking events. Panchkula has attracted more than 2,800 entries, including several established international players such as Sreeja Akula, Diya Chitale, Syndrela Das, Payas Jain, Manav Thakkar, Manush Shah, Ankur Bhattacharya, G Sathiyan and Harmeet Desai.For many players, the issue is particularly relevant as the domestic calendar feeds into selection and ranking considerations. The withdrawal of ranking points means the Panchkula event will not carry the same significance for players seeking to improve their national standings.International player Ankur Bhattacharya said the change had come after players had already invested considerable time and resources in preparation.“We train day in and day out to perform at these national rankings. Taking away ranking points right before the tournament makes all our hard work, intense preparation, and severe financial investments meaningless. It feels like our careers are being toyed with,” he said.Youth player Suhana Saini also said the uncertainty had made planning difficult.“This decision is a massive setback for all players, especially those trying to improve their standings before the international cycles. We are completely stranded and cannot plan our schedule. It is incredibly demotivating for the entire player community,” she said.Members of the table tennis fraternity have also sought clarity on the timing of the decision, coming nearly two months after the TTFI suspension.With the 2027 Olympic qualification cycle approaching and a packed international calendar ahead, including the Asian Championship, WTT Feeder Chennai, ITTF Mixed Team World Cup and World Youth Championship, players are keen for greater certainty over the domestic pathway.For Manika, meanwhile, Panchkula represents a return to the domestic circuit, one that could assume importance as she looks ahead to the next phase of her international career.
Article Summary: Manika Batra set to return to the national circuit. The 31-year-old will enter the National Ranking Table Tennis Championships in Panchkula, Haryana. It will be her first domestic appearance since the Senior Nationals in Shillong in April 2022.

Article Title: 33 teams, no relegation, 198 matches: Mumbai football's Elite Division raises eyebrows
Article Text:
MFA Elite Division raises eyebrows

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Mumbai’s top-flight football league is set to enter a season of unprecedented proportions, and not necessarily for the right reasons.The Mumbai Football Association’s (MFA) Elite Division, which kicks off on Oct 15, will feature 33 teams, a number virtually unheard of for a top division. What’s more, there will be no relegation for three years. At the end of that period, the division could have as many as 39 teams.The bloated league is the result of the MFA’s decision to merge its Private and Corporate leagues. The Corporate league had complained of being treated as a second-class competition, with poor scheduling and matches often confined to barely three months, making it difficult for companies such as Western Railway and Indian Navy to commit teams. Rather than address those concerns, the MFA opted for a merger.The 33 teams will be split into three groups of 11, with the top four from each advancing to a playoff stage comprising two groups of six. The top four will then enter the semifinals and final. In all, 198 matches will need to be staged.But venues and scheduling pose another concern. While the MFA is fighting to retain the Neville D’Souza ground, it has secured Cooperage for matches.At time slots of 10 am and 12 noon! When Mumbai’s heat and humidity are at their peak. AFC A-licensed coach Raj Shekar told TOI: “We must consider Mumbai’s heat and humidity and whether this is sustainable for players, clubs and spectators if we want to make the league popular.Shekar also questioned the 51.5% increase in the entry fee, saying it had, to his understanding, neither been approved by the president nor placed before the executive committee.Ex-India captain Godfrey Pereira was blunt: “It’s an absolute mess and definitely not something that should happen. How will it help grow the sport? Without relegation, what’s there to fight? The quality will deteriorate.”Sudhakar Rane, MFA secretary, told TOI that it’s the best they could do. “Teams in the corporate league were complaining, so we thought that this was the best solution. About the ground, these slots were the only ones available so there’s nothing we can do about it.”
Article Summary: Mumbai's top-flight football league is set to enter a season of unprecedented proportions. The Mumbai Football Association’s (MFA) Elite Division, which kicks off on Oct 15, will feature 33 teams. There will be no relegation for three years. At the end of that period, the division could have as many as 39 teams.

Article Title: 'Real-life hero': Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh lead cricket fraternity in hailing Captain Smit Machchhar after saving 174 lives
Article Text:
Smit Machchhar

'A true real-life hero': Sachin Tendulkar

Raina hails 'son of Gujarat'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sehwag praises his courage under pressure

Yuvraj: 'Some moments show you what a person is truly made of'

NEW DELHI: The courage of Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who was seriously injured while trying to prevent a potential catastrophe aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073, has earned admiration from across the country, including some of India's biggest cricketing names.Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh, Suresh Raina and Virender Sehwag were among the former India cricketers who took to social media to salute Machchhar for his bravery and presence of mind during the terrifying mid-air incident.Machchhar was the captain of the Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight when a violent confrontation reportedly broke out in the cockpit on Wednesday. According to reports, he was attacked by his co-pilot but, despite suffering serious injuries, managed to help open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew members to intervene. The aircraft was subsequently diverted and landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 174 people aboard were reported safe.Tendulkar was among the first prominent cricketers to acknowledge Machchhar's courage."Learnt about the incredible bravery of Captain Smit Machchhar. Immense courage in the face of a terrifying and unprecedented challenge. A true real-life hero. The entire world is proud of you," Tendulkar wrote.Former India batter Suresh Raina also paid tribute to Machchhar, highlighting the captain's courage despite being seriously injured."A true hero, a proud moment for India! Salute to Captain Smit Machchhar, a son of Gujarat, whose extraordinary courage and presence of mind, even while seriously injured, helped save 174 precious lives," Raina wrote.Virender Sehwag highlighted the extraordinary circumstances in which Machchhar continued to act despite his injuries."In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others," Sehwag wrote.Yuvraj Singh also joined the tributes, focusing on Machchhar's decision to put the safety of others ahead of his own."Some moments show you what a person is truly made of," Yuvraj wrote.Machchhar, who has more than 13 years of commercial flying experience and previously worked with SpiceJet before joining flydubai in 2022, is currently recovering after undergoing treatment in Saudi Arabia.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured while trying to prevent a potential catastrophe aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073. Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh, Suresh Raina and Virender Sehwag took to social media to pay tribute to the pilot's bravery. All 174 people aboard the flight were reported safe.

Article Title: 'We will replicate this at Olympics': BFI chief hails India's boxing show at Asian Games
Article Text:
Lovlina Borgohain (Image credit: X)

Six medals from 11 events

‘Performance can be replicated at Olympics’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Priya, Narender and Kapil settle for bronze

Three chances for gold

India’s strong boxing campaign at the Asian Games has given the Boxing Federation of India (BFI) confidence ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.BFI president Ajay Singh praised the Indian boxers after the team secured six medals from 11 events, including three finalists. He said the Asian Games field is close to what boxers face at the Olympics.India added three more bronze medals on Wednesday through Priya Ghanghas, Narender and Kapil Pokhariya, who lost their respective semifinal bouts.Lovlina Borgohain, Ankush Dahiya and Parveen Hooda have already reached their respective finals and will fight for gold.“We've got six medals in this Asian Games out of 11 events. Last time we got four medals out of 13 events that were held. So we've done considerably better than the last time,” Singh said.He also pointed out that three Indian boxers reaching the finals was a big achievement given the quality of competition at the Asian Games.“The fact that three boxers are in the finals now, I think, is an incredible achievement given that the Asian Games for boxing is very similar to the Olympics,” he said.Singh believes the performance in the Asian Games can give a clear indication of what India can achieve at the Olympics.“All the top countries in the world are in the Asian Games. So whatever performance we are doing here, it's very possible that this will be replicated in the Olympics,” he said.“So getting six medals, out of which three are now in the finals, is an incredible achievement. And we are hoping that tomorrow or day after, when the finals are held, we convert some of those finalists into golds,” he added.Priya, the reigning Commonwealth Games champion, lost 1-4 to China's Yang Chengyu in the women's 60kg semifinal. Priya attacked from the start but could not do enough to convince the judges across the three rounds.Narender also finished with a bronze medal in the men's +90kg category. He lost 0-5 to Kazakhstan's reigning world champion Oralbay in the semifinal.Kapil's campaign ended with a bronze medal after he lost 1-4 to Uzbekistan's world champion Turabek Khabibullaev in the men's 90kg semifinal.India still have three boxers in the fight for gold. Lovlina booked her place in the women's 75kg final after beating Kazakhstan's Natalya Bogdanova 3-2 in a close semifinal.Parveen and Ankush have also reached their respective finals.India will therefore have three chances to add gold medals to its boxing tally on October 2.
Article Summary: India secured six medals from 11 events, including three finalists. Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh said the Asian Games field is close to what boxers face at the Olympics. India added three more bronze medals on Wednesday through Priya Ghanghas, Narender and Kapil Pokhariya.

NEW DELHI: India’s emphatic eight-wicket win over West Indies in the second ODI came with an injury concern as fast bowler Prasidh Krishna suffered a hamstring strain and could bowl only five overs in Guwahati. India are monitoring the pacer’s condition, with scans scheduled to assess the extent of the injury on Thursday.Prasidh returned figures of 1/45 from his five overs after pulling up during his spell as West Indies posted a record 405/7. India subsequently chased down the target in just 43.3 overs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed after the match that Prasidh was dealing with a hamstring strain and would undergo further assessment."Prasidh Krishna has a strain in the hamstring, he is being monitored. They will do scans and we will have an update by tomorrow evening," Kotak said.The injury could force India to make a change for the series finale in Mullanpur on Saturday. Prasidh is not part of the squad for the five-match T20I series against West Indies beginning in Lucknow on October 6.Naman Dhir also had to leave the field after twisting his ankle while bowling 6.1 overs, but Kotak played down concerns over the all-rounder, saying the issue was related to cramps."Naman is someone who normally doesn't get cramps, but it can happen," he said.Dhir had taken on an increased bowling workload after Prasidh's curtailed spell, while India’s other bowlers struggled to contain a West Indies batting line-up that piled up 405 runs.The injury concerns came after a remarkable batting-dominated contest in which more than 800 runs were scored and five centuries were recorded, including Shubman Gill’s double hundred and Rohit Sharma’s century.With the nature of the pitch drawing criticism, Kotak said there was no such thing as a perfect surface in cricket."When we talk about pitches, see, I don't think anyone in the world can make a so-called 'perfect pitch'," Kotak said."You can never say this wicket will have 250 or 300 runs. There will always be criticism (there is a batting collapse curators will be criticised and vice-versa when it turns out to be a belter)," he said.Kotak also pointed to the changing standards of ODI batting, noting how 183 was once a formidable total in the 60-over era before modern batting has pushed expectations towards 400-plus scores."So whether it is only the wicket to blame or the standard of batting is going high, the way guys are batting, it's debatable," he said."But yes, there will be a time when we'll have difficult wickets in one-day games also, and different venues will have different wickets. So hopefully by then we should be prepared."Kotak credited India’s top order for turning what initially appeared to be a daunting chase into a routine pursuit.Rohit and Gill added 255 for the opening wicket in only 26.2 overs before Virat Kohli contributed 29 off 19 balls. Gill remained unbeaten on 223 as India reached 406/2 in 43.3 overs."It's one of the best I have seen in ODI cricket," Kotak said of the Rohit-Gill partnership."It's one of the best I have seen in ODI cricket," he said about Rohit-Shubman's 255-run opening wicket stand that came in just 26.2 overs."The way we batted -- Shubman and Rohit started, and then Kohli also contributed. By 32 overs, 320 runs, the game was more or less over."Kotak also praised Gill’s hunger to convert his century into a huge score despite the heat and humidity."I feel players have that hunger. Article Title: Shubman Gill scripts history, becomes first captain to score double centuries in Test and ODIs
Article Text:
Shubman Gill scripts cricket history

From Edgbaston 269 to Guwahati 223*

Fastest double century in ODI history

Poll Vote & Share your view Which aspect of Gill's performance was most impressive? Fastest double century Chasing down 406 runs Consistency across formats 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Shubman Gill did not just produce another breathtaking innings on Wednesday night. He created a record that had never been achieved in international cricket before.The Indian captain smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls against West Indies in the second ODI in Guwahati, becoming the first captain to score a double century in both Test and ODI cricket. Gill had previously scored 269 against England at Edgbaston in 2025, making his latest feat a unique chapter in the history of captaincy.What made the Guwahati innings even more remarkable was the situation. West Indies had posted 405/7, their first-ever 400-plus ODI total, after centuries from John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo. India then chased down 406 in just 43.3 overs, winning by eight wickets with 39 balls to spare.Gill's latest record cannot be viewed in isolation. In July 2025, while leading India in the Test series against England, he produced historic innings at Edgbaston. His 269 off 387 balls became the highest score by an Indian captain in Test cricket and the highest score by an Indian captain in a Test in England.That innings already placed Gill in an exclusive group of captains to score Test double centuries in England.Now, with his Guwahati double century, he has added an unprecedented ODI achievement to that record. Gill became the first captain to score a double century in both Test and ODI cricket.Gill reached his double century in just 117 balls, breaking Ishan Kishan's previous record of 126 balls. His 223* also became the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase, surpassing Glenn Maxwell's unbeaten 201 against Afghanistan.By the time he reached 223, Gill had hit 26 fours and eight sixes, finishing with the highest ODI score of his career. His previous best was the 208 he scored against New Zealand in Hyderabad in 2023.That makes Gill only the second Indian after Rohit Sharma to score multiple ODI double centuries. Rohit remains the only batter with three ODI double tons.Gill's individual brilliance came during a chase that itself entered the record books. India's 406/2 became their highest successful ODI chase, surpassing their previous record. It was also only the second time a team had successfully chased a target of 400 or more in men's ODI cricket, after South Africa's famous 438-run chase against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006.The foundation was laid by Gill and Rohit Sharma, who put together a remarkable 255-run opening partnership. Rohit contributed 101 before being dismissed, leaving Gill to complete the chase alongside Ruturaj Gaikwad.The match therefore produced an unusual statistical symmetry: West Indies made 405, three of their batters scored centuries, and India chased the target with two centuries of their own.The Guwahati double century also took Gill to his 11th ODI century in just 68 innings. He became the fastest Indian to reach 11 ODI hundreds, moving ahead of Virat Kohli's mark of 82 innings. Hashim Amla remains the fastest overall, having reached the milestone in 64 innings.
Article Summary: Shubman Gill becomes the first captain to score a double century in both Test and ODI cricket. Indian captain smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls against West Indies in Guwahati. West Indies had posted 405/7, their first-ever 400-plus ODI total, after centuries from John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo. India then chased down 406 in just 43.3 overs, winning by eight wickets.

GUWAHATI: Shubman Gill produced a breathtaking batting masterclass to smash the fastest double century in ODI cricket history as India chased down West Indies’ imposing 406-run target with 39 balls to spare in the second ODI at Barsapara Cricket Stadium here on Wednesday. The eight-wicket win, second on the trot, also sealed the three-match series in the hosts’ favour.Gill remained unbeaten on 223 (133 balls, 28x4, 8x6) eclipsing Ishan Kishan’s previous mark of a 126-ball double century against Bangladesh. It was Gill’s second ODI double ton, after his 208 against New Zealand in Hyderabad in 2023, leaving him behind only Rohit Sharma, who has three, on the list of Indian batters with multiple double centuries.Reaching 200-run mark (117 balls), Gill had earlier raced to his 11th ODI century in just 62 balls, setting the tone for an extraordinary assault. He continued to find boundaries at will, combining precise cuts and drives with powerful strokes all around the park as India kept the pressure firmly on the West Indies attack.At the other end, Rohit Sharma provided the perfect launchpad with a 101 off 75 balls. The opener completed his 35th ODI century and, in the process, crossed 12,000 runs in the format, becoming only the third Indian after Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli and the seventh batter overall to reach the milestone.Rohit was dismissed immediately after reaching three figures, trapped lbw by Jayden Seales. He had earlier been given a reprieve on 84 when Keacy Carty dropped him at deep mid-wicket. Gill and Rohit’s opening stand of 255 runs fell just three runs short of Sachin Tendulkar and Sourav Ganguly’s all-time record of 258 runs scored against Kenya in 2001.Virat Kohli made 29 before falling while attempting to guide a bouncer. Gill, however, remained in complete command. His unbeaten knock carried India to 406/2 and their highest successful ODI chase, surpassing their previous best of 362/1 against Australia in Jaipur in 2013. The victory was also the highest successful chase on Indian soil and the second-highest successful chase in ODI cricket. South Africa’s 438/9 against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006 remains the benchmark.India’s remarkable pursuit followed an extraordinary batting display from Windies, who posted 405/7 — their highest ODI total against India. For the first time in their ODI history, three West Indies batters scored centuries in the same innings. John Campbell struck 101 off 68 balls (9x4, 5x6), captain Shai Hope made 104 off 94 (8x4, 3x6), while Amir Jangoo top-scored with a 114 off 77 (13x3, 3x6)

Article Title: Asian Games: India win women’s team squash bronze after Anahat Singh’s heartbreak

NEW DELHI: India added another squash medal to their impressive Asian Games 2026 haul as the women’s team settled for bronze after a hard-fought 1-2 semifinal defeat to Hong Kong on Thursday.The result took India’s squash medal tally at the Aichi-Nagoya Games to four, with Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh having earlier won silver medals in the singles events, while Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar had claimed bronze in mixed doubles.India still have another opportunity to add to that tally later on Thursday, with the men’s team semifinal scheduled for later in the day.A lot rested on 18-year-old Anahat in the opening match against Hong Kong’s Sin Yuk Chan. The world No. 17 Indian appeared in control after winning the first two games 11-9, 11-8, but the contest dramatically slipped away from her.Anahat led 10-6 in the fourth game and had four match points, but could not close out the match. Chan fought back to win the game 13-11 before taking the deciding game 12-10 to complete a 3-2 victory.Anahat had also recovered from a 7-9 deficit in the fifth game to level it at 9-9. Chan earned the first match point, which Anahat saved with a backhand drop, but the Hong Kong player remained composed, earned another match point and converted it to put Hong Kong 1-0 ahead.With India facing elimination, Tanvi Khanna produced an excellent fightback against Ka Yi Lee.The Indian lost the opening game 4-11 but gradually found her rhythm, extending rallies and forcing Lee into errors. Tanvi edged a tense second game 13-11 after saving opportunities and then fought back from 3-7 down in the third to win it 11-9.The fourth game followed another dramatic pattern. Tanvi led 4-1 before Lee moved ahead 9-7. The Indian fought back, saved a game point and eventually converted her second match point to complete a 3-1 victory — 4-11, 13-11, 11-9, 13-11 — and level the tie.That left the outcome in the hands of veteran Joshna Chinappa, but Hong Kong's Ho Tze Lok proved too strong in the deciding match.The former world top-10 player struggled to match her opponent physically and lost the opening two games. Joshna then found some momentum late in the third, saving five match points, but Ho eventually closed out the contest 11-4, 11-7, 11-9 in just 21 minutes.The defeat ended India's hopes of reaching the women's team final, but the bronze adds to what has already been a highly productive squash campaign at Aichi-Nagoya.

Article Title: EXCLUSIVE | Kynan Chenai's golden charm: How father's 30-year-old gun helped him win Asian Games gold

'He's been one of my biggest inspirations'

From Rio to another Asian Games gold

'I'm more hungry now'

NEW DELHI: When Kynan Chenai arrived at the Aichi Prefectural General Shooting Gallery in Aichi-Nagoya for the Asian Games 2026 trap mixed team final, the gun in his hands was not his regular weapon.It was a 30-year-old gun borrowed from his father, Darius Chenai.Darius, a two-time national trap champion, had used the same barrel to win both his national titles. On Wednesday, his son used it to win the mixed team trap gold medal with Neeru Dhanda.For Kynan, the medal was special. Tears rolled down his cheeks when the national anthem was played. Winning the gold became even more special because it came with the gun that carries his father's legacy of more than three decades.In a big final, Kynan did not know that his lucky charm would turn into a golden charm.“I did shoot with my father's barrel. It's a very old barrel. He got it with his first import that he shot the national championship with. And he's won two national championships in India with this barrel itself,” Kynan toldin an exclusive interview from Japan.The decision to change his gun came at the last moment. His coach asked him to switch weapons, and instead of looking for another option, Kynan approached his father and decided to use the barrel with which Darius had won two national titles.“I didn't have one with me at the time and the coach wanted me to change, so I took his. And yeah, actually, if you think about it, it's a very special feeling to have this medal with that barrel. And I'm not giving it back to him anytime soon,” he said.Darius has played a big role in his son's career. From making sure Kynan remained focused on academics to supporting his journey in shooting, he has been a constant presence in his life.“He's been one of my biggest inspirations and, more importantly, the biggest support in my shooting career for the last 25 years. He has nurtured me from a young age till now,” Kynan said.Even before the Asian Games final, Kynan turned to his father for advice.“Even yesterday, we had a long chat about what the plan was and how I'm going to go about my final and the upcoming season. You know, all the doubts and all the questions you have as an athlete. I was having a chat with him, in fact,” he said.For Kynan, it is simple: when in doubt or ahead of an important competition, pick up the phone and call his father. That is exactly what he did before the Asian Games mixed team final.“You know, he just settles you. He just gives you a base. Family always gives you a base,” Kynan said.Kynan represented India at the 2016 Rio Olympics, where he finished 19th in the men's trap event. He then missed out on qualification for the Tokyo and Paris Olympics.But his hunger for another Olympic appearance, and winning a medal, remains strong.“Yeah, every Olympics you miss is a big thing. And, well, for Tokyo and Paris, I simply didn't win a quota. And when you don't win a quota, you don't go to the Olympics,” he said.“I went to the Paris Olympics as a spectator. And watching my fellow shooters shoot gave me a push. I went with Rajeshwari (wife) for the Paris Olympics, and it was really nice to be on the Olympic ground, watch people shoot and be a spectator,” he said.“It also gives you a little bit of a push to train harder and try and win a quota for the country again,” he added.Kynan now has his eyes on the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.“Well, it is a goal, but if God has it in His plan and it's written in the stars, then yes,” he said.Kynan has now won gold at two consecutive Asian Games editions. He was part of India's men's trap team that won gold at Hangzhou 2022, while also winning an individual bronze. He has now added the mixed team trap gold in Aichi-Nagoya.With every medal, Kynan says his hunger to win more has only grown.“I'm more hungry now because I feel like I've done a lot of work over the decade, but this sport never ceases to amaze me. And I'm just happy that I could stick to my guns, stick to my process and carry out the mixed team. The way it went down today was really rewarding,” he said.“So I'm more hungry, I think, and I'll always be hungry because this sport is an obsession. It's nothing else,” he added.Neeru had to fight through illness to win her Asian Games medals.Just days before the Games, she suffered from viral fever. She took medicines for a few days, but when her condition did not improve, she was admitted to PSRI Hospital in Chirag Delhi. She was later discharged, but had little time to recover before competition.According to Kynan, Neeru was still not fully fit, but she fought bravely and gave it everything.Despite not being able to train in the lead-up to the competition, Neeru won the individual trap gold on Tuesday. She had already helped India secure a silver in the women's team event before teaming up with Kynan to win mixed team gold on Wednesday.The Indian pair finished with an Asian and Games record score of 34.“She was just brilliant. She didn't do any training leading up to the tournament, and she was in hospital. And then she came out and shot that final yesterday in the rain. She was really tired today, but she held on as much as she could, and it was great,” Kynan said.“You need a partner to hold on and fight for every target, which she did, and we have a result,” he added.Before the final, Kynan had only one message for his partner.“Ahead of the final, I just said to her: ‘Good luck, be strong and just keep shooting. That's it.’”
Article Summary: Kynan Chenai won gold at the Asian Games 2026 trap mixed team final. He used a 30-year-old gun borrowed from his father, Darius Chenai. Darius, a two-time national trap champion, had used the same barrel to win both his national titles.

Before the Asian Games, Harita Bhadra had a fairly modest definition of success. A personal best, she had said, would make her happy. A podium finish was what she wanted to chase.She will now leave Aichi-Nagoya with two bronze medals - one from the women’s 200m and another from the mixed 4x100m relay, where she ran the anchor leg as India set a national record of 41.06 seconds.“I’m very happy because I got like two medals at the end of the day. Getting on the podium is like one of the best feelings, especially when you’re representing India, and you’re getting a medal for your country. So that was a very surreal experience for me,” Bhadra told Timesofindia.com from Japan.“And I didn’t get a personal best, but considering the weather conditions and everything, I feel like I gave my best. So that’s okay,” she added.It was also Bhadra’s first senior international competition representing India. She had not been through a junior international programme in Indian colours before arriving in Japan, so much of what she encountered in Aichi-Nagoya was new - the scale of the stadium, the pressure of the races and the closeness of the competition - but she found out quickly that training cannot reproduce all of that.“I’ve definitely learned a lot from this competition and definitely even discovered a lot about myself actually,” she said.“Such scenarios [can be experienced] only in competition, and the level of the pressure and the level of execution will only increase as you go higher and higher.”“But I discovered how strong I can be mentally. If I tell my mind to do something, it can do it.”Watching Bhadra through the Games, there was a noticeable contrast. Before the races, she was quiet and composed, but her expressions would change once she crossed the line. The happiness was immediate.“On the start line, my only mindset is that I belong over here,” she replied when asked what he goes through between those two moments.“I don’t have to be scared of any of my competitors because, even I’m on the same start line. I just try to trust my body, and I’m not thinking about anything because I’m just staying in the moment, and I’m just trusting my body that all the work I have done is like my body is ready to execute it.”That composure, however, did not mean the nerves had disappeared before her 200m final. Rather, Bhadra says she was nervous. The Reliance Foundation-backed athlete had already given herself a good platform in the heats, finishing second with 23.31s, behind Singapore’s Shanti Pereira.“Everybody on the start line is nervous, but you just accept it. You’re nervous, but that doesn’t mean you’re not confident at the same time. It’s just a mix of both things: you can be nervous but also be equally confident at the same time.”The finish, though, was nerve-racking - to say the least. Pereira won in 22.78s, with China’s Chen Yujie taking silver in 22.93s. Bhadra crossed in 23.20s, but Japan’s Abigeirufuka Ido was only 0.01 seconds behind in 23.21s. That meant the bronze was decided by the narrowest of margins, with the photo finish separating Bhadra from the Japanese sprinter.For a few seconds after the finish, Bhadra was unsure where she had finished. She had expected the results to appear on the screen opposite the finish line. After the race, she went across to teammate Unnati Aiyappa and sat with her. Unnati eventually pointed towards another screen. “She was like, ‘You have come third’, and that’s when I realised that I have come third.”The medal was secure, but the race itself still had things Bhadra wanted to improve. “You will never be satisfied with a race. There is always something you will feel that, okay, this could have been done better. This part could have been executed better,” she said.For the 23-year-old, more international exposure should help with that. The stage was completely new, and she felt there were sections of the race she could have handled better.“I know I had more left in me, but I trust the process, and I trusted that whenever I know I can, I will execute that race that I have in my mind.”One part of the race, though, had given her evidence that the work was moving in the right direction. The last 30 metres, something which had worked on, with her coach Rohit Mane at Reliance Foundation.“Yes, definitely, because I think I won the race because of the last 30 metres. So that improvement was clearly there.”Bhadra’s coach Mane was not in Japan for the Games, but they stayed in touch through video calls and regular calls, while the relay group had the support of Reliance Foundation’s Martin Owens and James Hillier, along with the AFI coaches, around them in Japan.The coaches, she said, kept reminding the four runners that the work had already been done and that they had to trust the runner alongside them. “They kept us motivated to like trust each other. And that's how we also trusted our partners more.”By the time Bhadra returned to the track for the mixed 4x100m relay, she had already raced twice. The stadium was no longer unfamiliar.“I was definitely more confident because I had, like, two races' experience,” she said. “I knew now how it’s going to feel like, on the start, and I knew how I will feel stepping into the stadium and everything, how the call room is.”“I was more calm and settled because I was familiar with the environment, basically. So going into the relay, I felt more collected than I was in 200.”The quartet of Gurindervir Singh, Sneha Shanuvali, Animesh Kujjur and Bhadra had been working on the event well before arriving in Nagoya. The Asian Games camp in Bhubaneswar in August, followed by an acclimatisation camp in Tsukuba.They trained the relay twice a week during the camp. As the Games approached, that came down to once a week because all four athletes also had individual events to prepare for.Bhadra ran the anchor leg in both the semifinal and final, producing strong finishes on each occasion. In the semifinal, she had to recover after a difficult baton exchange on the bend, but still produced the run that carried India into the final. In the medal race, her late surge again proved crucial as India secured bronze. The decision to use Bhadra as the anchor, she says, was made by the coaching staff and AFI team.“They decided to give me the anchor leg. So I was like, okay, I will do the anchor leg. That’s it.”The semifinal did test that decision almost immediately. Kujur fell during the baton exchange before Bhadra took the baton and glanced back for a fleeting second, but with the baton in hand, she focused on the job at hand.“My only thing was I have got the baton. So he [Kujur] has done his job of giving me the baton. So my job is to make the team qualify. As soon as I finished, I was just looking out, like just trying to understand what actually happened. I was trying to see if Animesh is okay or what actually happened.”There was another decision from earlier in the year that Bhadra had wanted to test properly: putting her studies on hold and giving sprinting her full attention.She had not made the decision because she could not handle both. She wanted to find out what would happen if she did not have to divide her time.“I just wanted to give myself the chance to explore how it would be like. I only have to just focus on track and I don’t have to juggle two things at once,” she said.Track, she said, requires time and dedication. “I am very happy with the decision. It was a good decision. I’m happy I gave myself the opportunity to explore how it would be.”Her family being in Japan made the week different too. She had wanted them to see her compete at a major event, and they were there for it.“I actually loved it that my family was there because I was just so excited that they are going to see me run at such a big event, like one of the biggest events of my athletics career so far,” she said.“I was very happy they could be there with me because it just made everything like 100 times more special.”Having ticked one of the big markers for this year, Bhadra is eyeing higher goals now, and her next target is already clear.“I am chasing to qualify for the World Championships in 2027.”The World Championships and eventually the Olympics, which had seemed further away before Aichi-Nagoya, now feel a little closer too. “Yes, definitely. It’s a step closer to, like, step higher, step closer. The qualifying mark is 22.45s for 200 metres.”She believes it is achievable. Bhadra’s personal best in 200m currently stands at 23.14s, which she clocked in June this year.“It is doable. But yeah, it is closer but still a lot of work to do there,” said Bhadra, pausing briefly before answering.The area she wants to work on most is not the one a stopwatch will immediately show. It is the mental side. “On the starting line, before even starting the race, if you are mentally not strong, you have lost the race. Everybody is so close, like I said, 0.01 seconds. Like, it’s like nothing.”Her answer is to stay calm enough to keep competing when the race is still there to be won. “You have to have that mental thing of not giving up, of believing that, ‘No, I can still win.’”For Bhadra, being mentally calm and connected to the race is now part of the work alongside the physical preparation. She is not planning to choose between the 100m and 200m just yet.The two events, she says, complement each other. Training for the 100m helps the 200m, and vice versa. She will take an off-season before her coach puts together the next plan.As for a favourite?“I have my days of choosing 100 and some days of choosing 200. I can’t choose for sure.”The medals have not changed the way she wants to approach the next season either. Before the Games, Bhadra had spoken about taking things one day at a time. She still uses the same approach now, even with the attention that will come after two Asian Games medals.“I really don’t think about expectations. Over there, I’m just running for myself. I’m not running for anybody else. The only thing is, yes, every day has to be an improvement, even if it is little. But my only goal is to take it one day at a time and to improve from the previous day,” she said.For now, there is no elaborate celebration planned. Her family is staying in Japan for a few more days to explore the country. Once she returns, Bhadra wants to meet her coach and ‘show off’ the two medals. Then there will be family and friends at home.And then there is Dagina.The handmade jewellery brand Bhadra started in October 2025 will turn one next month. She designs and makes the pieces herself and, because it remains a hobby, handles the work on her own. The Asian Games build-up and the last two months in camp meant she had not been able to spend much time on it.She had started Dagina as a way of taking her mind away from athletics. Now Japan has given her an idea for what comes next.“Now, once I’m back, I’m going to start again, maybe do a collection inspired by Japan or something like that.”
Article Summary: Harita Bhadra won two bronze medals at the Asian Games 2026. The 200m bronze came down to 0.01 seconds from Japan’s Abigeirufuka Ido. She ran the anchor leg as India set a national record of 41.06 seconds in the 4x100m relay.

NEW DELHI: India moved up to eighth place in the Asian Games medal standings after reaching the 10-gold mark on Wednesday, with a golden sweep by the compound archers and another gold in shooting powering a big jump in the table.India now have 60 medals - 10 gold, 21 silver and 29 bronze.The compound archers won gold in all three team events, while Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai added another gold in the mixed team trap event. Three boxing bronzes and Sunil Kumar's wrestling bronze also contributed to India's tally.India's 10 gold medals have lifted them to eighth in the standings, with Bahrain seventh on 11 golds. India have 60 medals overall, while Kazakhstan are ninth with 56 medals, including nine golds.China continue to lead the table with 275 medals - 150 gold, 66 silver and 59 bronze. Japan are second with 199 medals, while South Korea are third with 102.The compound archers were the stars of the day, winning gold in the men's, women's and mixed team events.Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep started the gold rush by winning the women's team title. They defeated China's Wunier, Yue Wang and Fangyao Wei 238-234.The Indian trio matched the world record with their score as they successfully defended their Asian Games title.Chikitha and Sahil Jadhav then won the mixed team gold after a thrilling final against South Korea's Jungyoon Park and Choi Eun Gyu. The Indian pair won 158-157 after a shoot-off.Kushal Dalal, Sahil and Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru completed the sweep by beating China's Jiahao Liao, Jinyi Liu and Jingyu Shi 238-237 in the men's team final.Chikitha and Sahil finished the day with two gold medals. The mixed team victory also secured an Olympic quota for India. India became the first country to qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics compound mixed team event, which will make its Olympic debut.At the shooting range, Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai recovered from a difficult start to win gold in the mixed team trap event.The Indian pair finished with a score of 34, setting an Asian and Games record. It was Neeru's second gold of the Games after she had earlier won the individual trap title. She had also helped India win silver in the women's team trap event.With two golds and a silver, Neeru has become the most successful Indian athlete at the ongoing Games.The four gold medals on Wednesday took India's gold tally to 10 and helped the country climb two places to eighth in the overall standings.
Article Summary: Compound archers win gold in all three team events. Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai add another gold in the mixed team trap event. Three boxing bronzes and Sunil Kumar's wrestling bronze also contributed to India's tally. India's 10 gold medals have lifted them to eighth in the standings.

Tough day in other sports

India had its best day of the Asian Games so far as compound archers won all three team gold medals, while shooters Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai also finished on top in the mixed trap event.Three bronze medals in boxing and wrestling took India’s overall tally to 60 medals - 10 gold, 21 silver and 29 bronze. India also moved up to eighth place from 10th on Tuesday.The compound archers were the stars of the day, successfully defending all three team titles.Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha and Prithika Pradeep started the gold rush by winning the women’s team event. They beat China’s Wunier, Yue Wang and Fangyao Wei 238-234. The Indian score equalled the world record.Chikitha and Sahil Jadhav then won the mixed team gold. They held their nerve against Korea’s Jungyoon Park and Choi Eun Gyu to win 158-157 after a shoot-off.The victory also helped India secure an Olympic quota place. India became the first country to qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics mixed team compound event, which will make its Olympic debut in Los Angeles.The men’s team of Kushal Dalal, Sahil and Ganesh Mani Ratnam Thirumuru completed the clean sweep.They beat China’s Jiahao Liao, Jinyi Liu and Jingyu Shi 238-237 in the final.Chikitha and Sahil finished the day with two gold medals each.At the shooting range, Neeru Dhanda and Kynan Chenai recovered from a difficult start to win the mixed trap gold.The Indian pair finished with a score of 34, setting an Asian and Games record.It was Neeru’s second gold of the Games. She had earlier won the individual trap gold and also played a key role in India’s silver medal-winning women’s trap team.With two golds and a silver, Neeru became the most successful Indian athlete at the ongoing Games.The Indian women’s hockey team also had a strong day, beating Korea 2-0 in the semifinal to reach the final.The victory assured India of at least a silver medal and improved on the bronze they won at the previous Asian Games.India’s boxers have already bettered their medal tally from the previous edition. They won four medals in Hangzhou, while six medals are assured this time.Lovlina Borgohain reached the women’s 75kg final after edging Kazakhstan’s Natalya Bogdanova, the reigning 70kg world champion, 3-2.However, Asian Games debutant Priya Ghanghas lost 1-4 to former world champion Yang Chengyu of China in the 60kg semifinal.Another debutant, Kapil, also lost 1-4 to Uzbekistan’s reigning world champion Turabek Khabibullaev in the 90kg semifinal.India will have three boxers fighting for gold on Friday — Lovlina, Parveen Hooda (65kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg).Priya, Kapil and super-heavyweight boxer Narender Berwal will return home with bronze medals.Sunil Kumar became the first Indian Greco-Roman wrestler to win two Asian Games medals after securing bronze in the men’s 87kg category.Sunil defeated the Philippines’ Roberts Callum Johnston 9-0 by technical superiority to secure a place on the podium.He had also won bronze at the Hangzhou Games, ending India’s 13-year wait for a Greco-Roman wrestling medal.Nisha Dahiya, however, finished without a medal in the women’s 68kg category.Both Indian squash teams booked their places in the semifinals and assured themselves of medals.The men’s team, the top seeds and defending champions, beat Kuwait 2-0 in the quarterfinals.Veer Chotrani defeated Bader Almogghrebi 12-10, 8-11, 11-0, 11-5, before Abhay Singh sealed the tie with an 11-3, 11-4, 11-8 win over Ammar Altamimi.The women’s team also won 2-0 against Singapore.Tanvi Khanna beat Au Yeong Wai Iynn 11-6, 4-11, 15-13, 11-1, while 18-year-old Anahat Singh defeated Au Yeong Wai Yhann 11-7, 11-3, 11-4.Veteran Joshna Chinappa did not need to play.Sumit Nagal was the only Indian to progress in the men’s singles, beating Uzbekistan’s Sergey Fomin 6-3, 6-2 to reach the quarterfinals.He will next face third seed Yibing Wu of China.Dhakshineswar Suresh lost 3-6, 4-6 to Chinese Taipei’s Chun-Hsin Tseng in the third round.India’s men’s doubles campaign also ended after N Sriram Balaji and Anirudh Chandrasekar lost to China’s Fumin Chiang and Tianhui Ziang 7-6(4), 6-7(7), 8-10.Yuki Bhambri and Dhakshineswar also lost their quarterfinal, going down 6-7(5), 3-6 to Chinese Taipei’s Yu-Hsiou Hsu and Chenjui Ho.India had a difficult day in canoeing, esports, sepaktakraw and cycling, with none of the Indian participants progressing beyond the preliminary stages.
Article Summary: India had its best day of the Asian Games so far as compound archers won all three team gold medals. Three bronze medals in boxing and wrestling took India’s overall tally to 60 medals - 10 gold, 21 silver and 29 bronze. India moved up to eighth place from 10th on Tuesday.

Article Title: India break Korean wall to storm into Asian Games women's hockey final, set up gold-medal clash with China
Article Text:

India’s women’s hockey team secured a medal at the 2026 Asian Games after beating South Korea 2-0 in the semifinal on Wednesday. The win assured India of at least a silver medal, but they will now aim for gold when they face defending champions China in the final on October 2.China reached the final after beating Japan 4-2 on penalties. India will now face China for the gold medal, with the winner also securing direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.India were dominant for long periods against South Korea but struggled to convert their chances, particularly from penalty corners in the first two quarters at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium.South Korea parked the bus as India maintained a high press and lurked around the opposition D. However, neither team could score in the first two quarters, raising the possibility of another semifinal being decided by a penalty shootout.India finally broke the deadlock in the 44th minute through a penalty corner. Deepika played the ball across to Ishika, who finished the move to put India into the lead.India doubled their lead three minutes later. Salima Tete collected a loose ball and carried it into the circle before passing towards the centre. The ball deflected off the stick of a South Korean defender and rolled into the goal, with the goal awarded to the Indian captain.The victory gives India a chance to win their first women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games since 1982.
Article Summary: India beat South Korea 2-0 in the semifinal of the 2026 Asian Games. The win assured India of at least a silver medal, but they will now aim for gold when they face defending champions China in the final. China reached the final after beating Japan 4-2 on penalties.

Article Title: Sports Ministry top brass to skip Asian Games, focus on BRICS Games
Article Text:
File photo of Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao. (ANI)

NEW DELHI: The higher-ranking Sports Ministry officials, including Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao, have cancelled their plans to travel to Aichi-Nagoya for the ongoing Asian Games . It has been reliably learnt that the top brass will remain in the country to oversee the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games on October 12-13 in Ahmedabad.Rao, who was scheduled to fly out to Japan on September 28, altered his plans keeping the importance of the BRICS Games in mind. An official from the sports ministry denied reports that the move came because of India's underwhelming show in Japan."Secretary Sports (Rao), being the senior-most officer of the Ministry decided to monitor the preparation of the Games, given the time left for the Games to begin, which would have been difficult to do from Japan. Therefore, he has cancelled his trip to the Asian Games," a source told TimesofIndia.com.It has also been learnt that the Sports Ministry had always intended to keep the officials contingent limited as part of an austerity drive. With the closing ceremony scheduled for October 4, Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) CEO Col. NS Johal is one of the highest-ranking officials available in Aichi-Nagoya.Organisation of the BRICS Games is being coordinated between the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS), the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the Gujarat government. Around 2,000 athletes, officials and other participants from nine countries, including China, Russia, Iran, Bolivia, are due to attend the non-competitive tournament. The focus of the Games will be on showcasing traditional and indigenous sports and cultural practices from BRICS nations.With India due to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030 and bidding to host the 2036 Olympics, both in Ahmedabad, successful hosting of the BRICS Games has been considered as critical for the country's image as a sporting nation.
Article Summary: The top brass will remain in the country to oversee the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games. The focus of the Games will be on showcasing traditional and indigenous sports and cultural practices from BRICS nations. Around 2,000 athletes, officials and other participants from nine countries, including China, Russia, Iran, Bolivia, are due to attend the non- competitive tournament.

Article Title: Final farewell? Ronaldo abruptly leaves Portugal camp, promises truth 'in due time' and wishes team-mates 'good luck'
Article Text:
Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo, wearing a wedding band, claps his hands during warmup before the Nations League soccer match between Portugal and Wales in Lisbon, Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026. (AP Photo/Armando Franca)

Ronaldo confirms he has left Portugal camp

Jorge Jesus had told Ronaldo he would not start against Denmark

Portugal's head coach Jorge Jesus speaks during a news conference in Copenhagen, Denmark, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026, ahead of their Nations League soccer match against Denmark. (Liselotte Sabroe/Ritzau Scanpix via AP)

Pedro Proença travelled to address the situation

A Bola

Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo arrives for training in Copenhagen, Denmark, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026, ahead of their Nations League soccer match against Denmark. (Liselotte Sabroe/Ritzau Scanpix via AP)

Ronaldo's retirement remains unconfirmed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cristiano Ronaldo has abruptly left Portugal’s national team camp one day before the UEFA Nations League meeting with Denmark, after a turbulent few days involving his role under new head coach Jorge Jesus. The 41-year-old confirmed his departure in a statement on Wednesday, saying he would reveal the reasons “in due time” while wishing Portugal and his team-mates good luck. Whether the decision marks a farewell to international football remains to be seen.Ronaldo confirmed his departure from the Portugal camp on Wednesday, September 30, in a statement posted on his official social media accounts. The announcement came as Jesus held a press conference ahead of Portugal’s match against Denmark in Copenhagen. The Portugal captain said his decision followed the coach’s comments and a conversation with Proença, who had changed his schedule to travel to Copenhagen as tensions over Ronaldo’s role in the team grew.“After the National Team coach's press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the National Team training camp,” Ronaldo wrote.He then indicated that he would explain what had happened at a later stage.“In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure from the national team, to which I have always dedicated myself.”Ronaldo finished by wishing Portugal and his team-mates well.“Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception.”The Portuguese Football Federation confirmed that Ronaldo had left the camp, while saying the remaining squad would continue preparing for the Denmark match and the subsequent Nations League fixture against Norway.Ronaldo was seen leaving Parken Stadium in a Portuguese Football Federation vehicle as his team-mates arrived for training, according to Portuguese newspaper A Bola. His private jet was also reported to have been preparing to take him away from Denmark. Reuters later reported that the aircraft had left Madrid for Copenhagen and was scheduled to return to the Spanish capital.Ronaldo remians Portugal's most-capped player and leading scorer, with 234 appearances and 146 goals for his country.The dispute developed after Ronaldo was left on the bench for Portugal's 2–1 Nations League victory over Norway.Jesus selected João Félix and Gonçalo Ramos in attack, with Ramos scoring Portugal's winning goal after Erling Haaland had equalised. Ronaldo warmed up during the second half but was not introduced.Jesus had previously said he wanted to manage Ronaldo's workload after the forward played almost 70 minutes against Wales in Portugal's opening Nations League match.Ronaldo then went directly to the dressing room after the Norway victory rather than joining his teammates in celebrating with the travelling supporters.The situation continued into Portugal's preparations for Denmark.Jesus said on Wednesday that Ronaldo would train with the team, while also confirming that he would not start against Denmark.“Yesterday, he did not refuse to train,” Jesus said.“Francisco Conceicao did not train because he was injured, and Joao Felix because we tried to ease his fatigue, while Cristiano did work in the gym. Today he will train. It is the fourth day, so he will train.”Jesus then explained the decision he had made over Ronaldo's role.“I can promise what I want. I am the coach. I told the player that he would not start the match, and that he would be on the substitutes' bench.”“If I need him for 30 minutes then he will play, and if I do not need him then he will not play.”Jesus also made clear that nobody would influence his selection.“No player will change my mind, neither him nor anyone else in football, not even any president, that will never happen.”Ronaldo left the camp after the press conference.The Portuguese Football Federation president changed his schedule and travelled to Copenhagen as the situation around Ronaldo and Jesus escalated.Proença held talks with the parties involved on Wednesday morning after the disagreement that followed Ronaldo's omission against Norway.Jesus had maintained that there was no major problem between himself and Ronaldo and said his conversations with the captain had been normal.Ronaldo, however, had missed three consecutive training sessions according to, despite Jesus saying shortly before his departure that he expected the forward to train.The Portuguese newspaper reported that Ronaldo left the Parken Stadium in a Portuguese Football Federation vehicle as his teammates arrived for training.His departure came only minutes after Jesus' press conference.Earlier reports had said Ronaldo was unhappy with the decision to leave him out against Norway and with the uncertainty surrounding his starting place against Denmark.Portugal now face Denmark on Thursday without Ronaldo in the squad, with the team leading Nations League Group A4 after two victories.Portugal have six points, three clear of both Denmark and Norway.Ronaldo's departure does not amount to an official retirement announcement. He has not said that he is ending his international career, while the Portuguese Football Federation has not announced his retirement.His final words before leaving camp, however, have prompted immediate questions because he said he would reveal the reasons for his decision later and then wished Portugal and all his teammates good luck.Ronaldo has spent more than two decades representing Portugal, becoming the country's record appearance holder and scorer while winning the 2016 European Championship and the 2019 Nations League. Whether Wednesday's decision represents another dispute that can eventually be resolved or the beginning of the end of his international career remains unanswered.For now, Ronaldo has said only that he will tell the Portuguese people the truth “in due time”.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has left Portugal's national team camp one day before the UEFA Nations League meeting with Denmark. The 41-year-old confirmed his departure in a statement on Wednesday, saying he would reveal the reasons ‘in due time’ Portugal's head coach Jorge Jesus had told Ronaldo he would not start against Denmark.

Article Title: Manchester City guilty of all financial breaches, Premier League confirms; expulsion threat looms
Article Text:
Pep Guardiola, the then Manager of Manchester City, poses for a photo with the Premier League title trophy following his team's victory during the Premier League match between Manchester City and West Ham United at Etihad Stadium on May 19, 2024 in Manchester, England. (Photo/Getty Images)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Manchester City have been found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period from 2009 to 2018, with an independent commission ruling that the club used commercial arrangements to inflate its revenues and reduce costs.The commission found that City arranged contracts with several commercial partners under which the companies paid only part of the agreed sponsorship fees. The remaining amounts were funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment and Development (ADUG), which owned the club.The commission also found that further arrangements funded by ADUG allowed City to record lower operating expenses than they actually incurred.According to the ruling, the arrangements artificially increased the club’s revenues and reduced its costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion) during the period under investigation. This meant City did not accurately report their income and expenditure under the Premier League and UEFA’s financial sustainability rules.The commission found that City would have breached spending limits "by a very substantial amount" if the club had reported its finances accurately.City were also found guilty on the majority of charges relating to their failure to cooperate with the Premier League’s investigation. The commission said the club had "made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the Premier League" during the four-year investigation.No sanction has been imposed yet and City have said they will appeal the decision. Under Premier League rules, the punishment can range from a fine or points deduction to expulsion from the division.Everton and Nottingham Forest were handed points deductions during the 2023/24 season for single breaches of the financial sustainability rules. If a similar penalty were applied to City for more than 100 charges, the club could face relegation.The ruling puts City’s place in the Premier League at risk and also raises questions over whether titles could be stripped."The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade," Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said in a statement on Tuesday."Now we have the commission's decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the league, our clubs and fans."The decision follows an investigation into alleged breaches that began before the Premier League charged City with more than 100 offences in 2023. A hearing by an independent commission began in September 2024 and concluded three months later.Since Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, took over the club in 2008, City have won eight Premier League titles, four FA Cups and seven League Cups. They also won the Champions League for the first time in 2023.City expressed "surprise" at the commission’s decision and said they would continue to challenge the findings."Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe," the club said in a statement."It's incredibly serious, the Premier League report is incredibly stark," said the British government's culture, media and sport secretary Lisa Nandy.
Article Summary: Manchester City have been found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. The club used commercial arrangements to inflate its revenues and reduce costs. No sanction has been imposed yet and City have said they will appeal the decision. Under Premier League rules, the punishment can range from a fine or points deduction to expulsion from the division.

Article Title: Brazil to bring security team to avoid Messi-like fiasco

The Brazil national football team has been assured of top-notch security by authorities in India, but the five-time world champions are not leaving anything to chance.An eight-member security delegation from Brazil will arrive in Kolkata before the national team to ensure that the star footballers are well protected when they step into the country.A star-studded Brazilian squad captained by Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) defender Marquinhos and including Real Madrid attacker Vinicius Junior, Barcelona forward Raphinha, and Arsenal pair Gabriel Magalhaes and Bruno Guimaraes will arrive in Kolkata on Oct 1.The Selecao will play a friendly against India on Oct 3.“Brazil will have a security team comprising experts and former Army officials,” a source who is involved in organisation of the match told. “They will be in Kolkata early on Wednesday, much before the team arrives. Thousands of fans were angry as their view of the star footballer was blocked by dozens of VIPs and organisers who were seen jostling for a selfie.“Extra precautions are being taken,” said another official.The hotel where Brazil will stay for three days will be turned into a fortress. According to sources, the Brazil football federation (CBF) has asked for a “secure training centre, situated no more than 25 minutes travelling time from the hotel and 24-hour security on all floors of the hotel where the team will stay.”At the stadium, restrooms and other public facilities are being renovated, while new fencing is being installed around the practice grounds as part of the security arrangements.Brazil played two friendlies against Australia as part of their Asia tour and are now headed to India for a historic clash against India. Article Title: Al Fursan-led consortium acquires Kerala Blasters FC from Magnum Group
Article Text:
Kerala Blasters FC Vibin Mohanan, third left, celebrates with teammates after scoring the second goal during Indian Super League (ISL) match between Kerala Blasters FC and Jamshedpur FC, In Kochi, Kerala. (PTI File Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOCHI: A consortium led by UAE-based Al Fursan Group has taken complete ownership of Kerala Blasters FC , one of the most popular clubs in the Indian Super League . The announcement was made at a news conference in Kochi on Tuesday. Club officials did not disclose the value of the transaction, but sources indicate that the deal is worth about Rs 120 crore, placing it among the largest foreign investments in Indian football in recent years.The takeover ends the tenure of Hyderabad-based Magnum Sports, which had owned and managed the club since 2016. Kerala Blasters CEO Abhik Chatterjee said the ownership transfer will be carried out in phases and is expected to be completed over the next eight months.Under the new arrangement, the club’s operations will be managed by Ofioh Sporty. Its CEO, Thameem Anvar, said the new owners have plans to develop a dedicated stadium for the Blasters. He added that more details would be revealed once “Project Blasters” is formally announced.There had been speculation that the club could shift its base to Kozhikode, but Chatterjee clarified that Kochi will remain Kerala Blasters’ home.The team will continue to play its home matches at the Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium. Addressing expectations for the upcoming season, he said the club’s ambition to win remains strong, though preparations are limited by time. He also confirmed that Ashley Westwood will continue as head coach and will take decisions on squad matters.Chatterjee dismissed reports suggesting that the Blasters’ opening home match could be postponed. He said delaying the fixture would be unfair to other teams because the league schedule has already been released.Al Fursan Group is understood to have backing from business interests connected to Sharjah’s ruling Al Qasimi family. Its entry gives a Gulf-based investment group control of a club with one of the largest fan bases in Indian football.The acquisition comes as Kerala Blasters prepare for the 2026-27 ISL season. Magnum Sports had been seeking a buyer, and interested parties completed financial, legal and operational due diligence before the sale was finalised.
Article Summary: consortium led by UAE-based Al Fursan Group has taken complete ownership of Kerala Blasters FC. Club officials did not disclose the value of the transaction, but sources indicate that the deal is worth about Rs 120 crore. The takeover ends the tenure of Hyderabad-based Magnum Sports, which had owned and managed the club since 2016.

Article Title: FIFA hits back at UEFA: Infantino's lawyers accuse European body of 'harassment'
Article Text:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino

What is the FIFA Forward Enterprise plan?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FIFA lawyers have accused UEFA of harassing president Gianni Infantino and urged a Florida judge to reject the European soccer body's request for evidence related to a proposed private investment plan involving the 2026 World Cup, news agency Assocuated Press reported.In a 21-page filing submitted late Monday (local time) to the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida, FIFA lawyers said UEFA was wrong to suggest that Infantino sought to personally profit from the project, which caused a backlash in July before being dropped within days.UEFA has since asked three courts, including courts in Manhattan and Miami, to authorize discovery as it seeks information to help prepare a possible criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland over alleged financial mismanagement. One of the requests targets Josh Kushner's New York-based investment firm, while another relates to FIFA's office base in Miami.“UEFA’s conduct demonstrates that its (court filing) was made in bad faith and for the purpose of harassment,” FIFA lawyers said in the filing.The filing also pointed to the Nov. 18 deadline for candidates to enter the FIFA presidential election, which will be held in March in Morocco. Infantino is seeking a fourth and final term that would keep him in office through 2031.“This court should reject any attempt to influence FIFA’s presidential election based on these grounds,” FIFA lawyers wrote.UEFA led the backlash against the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which was proposed by Infantino. The plan involved creating a new FIFA subsidiary and selling at least 20% of FIFA's future commercial rights for $4.2 billion to a group of investors led by Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.UEFA said in court filings last month that the proposed valuation was a “fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit.” The claim came amid speculation that Infantino could take a CEO-like role at the new subsidiary with a salary higher than his current $6 million presidential pay package.FIFA lawyers rejected that suggestion, saying UEFA “falsely asserts that Mr. Infantino sought to have a personal financial interest in the FFE project.”The plan was first reported by the media on July 28. It led to criticism from FIFA's then-chief operating officer Kevin Lamour, who was later removed from his position. Infantino's senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro, a former Goldman Sachs partner, also resigned in protest, saying the deal was bad for soccer.Infantino later apologised for errors in the way the plan was handled and offered to open an independent external review of FIFA's governance.FIFA has maintained that the proposed commercial spinoff was intended to accelerate the development of soccer around the world, particularly outside Europe's wealthier football markets.
Article Summary: FIFA lawyers have accused UEFA of harassing president Gianni Infantino. They have urged a Florida judge to reject the European soccer body's request for evidence related to a proposed private investment plan involving the 2026 World Cup. UEFA led the backlash against the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which was proposed by Infantinos.UEFA has since asked three courts, including courts in Manhattan and Miami, to authorize discovery.
